events.credibility_reason: Scholze and Stix (2018) identified a defect at the Theorem 3.11 to Corollary 3.12 step, disputed by Mochizuki; the 2026 LANA interim report says the step cannot be formalised as written. Concerns n = 3 (abc), which the statement's 'more than three integers' excludes.

Origin of the construction is attributed inconsistently (README, PROOF.md, Redhill docstring); unexplained 'supplied' 20/19 and 180/179 constructions leave unclear whether n = 4 was open for the Ramaekers variant.
events.ai_basis: The Lean proof itself was written by GPT-6 Astra, as described below.

why: The statement names the n conjecture as the generalization of abc to more than three integers, i.e. the Browkin–Brzeziński conjecture for n ≥ 4; I read it as that standard statement, not the family of strong variants. On that reading the 1994 lower-bound half is a pre-snapshot case (journal of record), and the upper half is untouched. Ramaekers' and Browkin's strong conjectures are different statements under stronger hypotheses, so the HKS 2024 disproof and the Sep 2026 n = 4 refutation are variants; their families lie in the standard class but give lower bounds below the already-known 2n−5, moving nothing. All abc (n = 3) work, including Mochizuki and the exceptional-set counts, falls outside 'more than three integers' and is variant. Pasten–Sepúlveda-Manzo is conditional on a size hypothesis and gives a much weaker form, so variant rather than bound. Lean ports (Redhill) are formalisations: none. The Adamczewski repository's AI role is answered from its own quote crediting GPT-6 Astra with the proof (generated); the Redhill port earns no AI credit, its docstring merely repeating the other event's attribution.
doubts: The close call is the reading of the statement: if the bullet were taken to include the Ramaekers strong variant, the HKS 2024 and Adamczewski 2026 events would be cases (refuting), the latter AI-credited. I followed the standard conjecture that the Wikipedia article and HKS identify as 'the n-conjecture'. The Adamczewski AI role is also uncertain: PROOF.md attributes the family to a bounded search over Pakovich–Zvonkin examples, so the model may only have written the Lean proof; moot for status since the event is a variant.
